subject: CTrain schedule system — track nodes, speed table, and train spawning logic
overview: GTA:SA includes a working metro/freight train system. Trains follow pre-baked node paths defined in trains.dat (located in data/). Each train runs on a fixed track with a fixed schedule. The player can enter trains as a passenger or board the cab. CTrain inherits from CAutomobile.

trains_dat_format.description: trains.dat defines the list of spawnable trains. Each line specifies the model name, track assignment, initial speed, and node start index.

train_track_nodes.description: Track geometry is a sequence of 3D node points. CTrain advances the train by computing t (fractional position) along the current segment and lerping position and heading between consecutive nodes.

fields.name: m_fTrackDistance
fields.description: Cumulative track distance from start to this node (metres)

fields.name: m_nFlags
fields.description: Node flags: bit 0 = stop station, bit 1 = speed reduction zone, bit 2 = loop endpoint

ms_nNumTrains.description: Number of currently active train instances (max 4)

ms_pTrain_array.description: Array of 4 CTrain* pointers (spawned by CTrafficLights)

ms_fTrainSpeed.description: Shared base speed (overridden per-track by trains.dat)

station_stops.description: When a train reaches a node flagged as a stop station (bit 0 of m_nFlags), it decelerates to 0, holds for a fixed dwell time (3000ms), then accelerates back to track speed. Doors open during the dwell period using the animated parts of the train model.

passenger_boarding.description: The player can enter a stationary train as a passenger via the standard vehicle entry code. The player is teleported to a seat bone in the train model. Trains use a different seat assignment table from cars — the cab and two passenger carriages are separate model LODs.
